heard: A solar observatory became history's greatest comet hunter. It was launched in 1995 for just a two-year mission. Then a command error sent it spinning into a silent, frozen, deep space blackout. Engineers pulled off a miracle recovery using reaction wheels as virtual gyroscopes. Its LASCO instrument blocks the solar glare with an artificial eclipse. That sun-blocking trick unlocked a staggering scale of discoveries. Citizen scientists combing through public data found over 5,000 comets. More than half of all known comets were found by a solar observatory.
